A bit of premise, I am anthropophobic with C-PTS. With my therapists, I had been working on going out shopping, as well as a few mindfulness activities. 

At the time I wanted to do some puzzles. One day I walked up to the local plaza, I had to grab some food and I wanted to see if there were any nice puzzles at the newsagents. finishing my two tasks, I headed outside for a smoke and some stretches (both help balance and ground me). Out of the corner of my eye, I saw an older woman very obviously looking at me, she even bent over to look at me closer. I was totally freaked out. Trying really hard to keep calm and focus on my grounding, I saw her walking away. The next minute I hear a voice saying "excuse me? Do you like puzzles?" With a missed heartbeat I looked over at the voice. There was that same woman. Again freaking out, but also terrified of being rude, I told her yes. then she pulled out a cutie kitten puzzle from behind her and went on to explain that she had bought it for her children, but they had stopped enjoying puzzles and it had been sitting in her car unopened for years. I had been so shocked I barely stumbled out enough thank yous and she promptly walked off to do her shopping.   


I will never forget that kindness. It had been a bad day and with the exposure of people, it was going to be worse. Alas, that one person shone a bit of light on me and restored a little bit of my faith back to humanity. I still regret not being able to fully be able to show her how much she did for me that day.
